channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

item.title: [DW] Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

item.title: [DW] Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

item.title: [DW] Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

item.title: [DW] Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
item.description: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

item.title: [EU Observer] Latvian PM holds onto power as Russia-Ukraine war shapes election
item.description: Despite its ordinary conduct, Russia's war still shaped Latvia's election in a new normal for Europe that most of us had hardly imagined just five years ago.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Explainer] Gas glut or supply crunch? And what it means for EU methane rules
item.description: The EU wants to delay its methane rules over worries they might disrupt gas imports in an already stressed market. Some analysts say even small changes would add to current price pressures, but a giant gas glut is coming and might arrive sooner rather than later.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Putin understands only strength’: EU envoy in Kyiv urges stronger air defences and hybrid-war response
item.description: Katarína Mathernová, the EU's ambassador to Ukraine, says Putin is boiling Kyiv 'like a frog', but she is determined to stay. She sees parallels between Hitler's Mein Kampf and Putin's essay which stated that Ukraine has no right to national existence, sovereignty or identity.

item.title: [DW] UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
item.description: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brazil’s cliff‑hanger election could rob EU of key ally in Latin America
item.description: Brussels is watching as one of the world’s largest democracies heads to the polls on Sunday (4 September), with climate resilience and the Trump administration’s influence in the Americas at stake.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] AI threatens to deepen gender gaps — unless women seize the tools, says computer expert
item.description: From biased hiring algorithms to disappearing administrative posts, Bieliková argues that women risk being hit hardest by AI unless they seize the tools early and push for fairer, more accountable systems.

item.title: [EU Observer] Orbánism without Orbán? Why Magyar picked a fight with Kyiv over the ‘Carpathian Eight’
item.description: Some expected a change in Hungary's pro-Russian foreign policy after Viktor Orbán’s fall. But they failed to take into account the domestic political pressures on Hungary's PM .

item.title: [DW] Bosnia election: New technology might have stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead voters, but the result remains unchanged
item.description: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning along ethnic lines.

item.title: [DW] Hundreds of French schools closed amid protests
item.description: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. More protests are planned for Tuesday.

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin’s nuclear threats no longer work
item.description: The weakening of Russian deterrence has global implications — and they are not all positive

item.title: [Politico Europe] Emmanuel Macron is most impressive world leader on AI, says Sam Altman
item.description: OpenAI CEO tells Decoded by POLITICO the French president is “extremely thoughtful and has been for a long time about where this is going.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany risks being drawn into ‘violent conflict’ with Russia, spy chief warns
item.description: The head of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency also cautioned that NATO countries must beware of Moscow's "little green men."

item.title: [Politico Europe] Suspected plague in Russia puts EU on alert
item.description: “We are aware of the reports concerning the laboratory incident in Russia, seemingly involving a pathogen-causing plague,” says European Commission spokesperson.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump cheers Bolsonaro Jr’s advance on Lula in Brazil, but EU fears for Mercosur alliance
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is the favourite to defeat president Lula in the second round of Brazil's presidential elections, which could mean disaster for EU-Latin America relations.

item.title: [Financial Times] Bond turbulence means it’s time for the ECB to put QT on hold
item.description: Prudence suggests a halt by the central bank until more stable conditions are restored

item.title: [Financial Times] Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez calls snap election
item.description: Move to hold vote on November 29 comes after government defeat on legislation aimed at ending housing crisis

item.title: [Financial Times] Brazil’s Bolsonaro dynasty closes in on stunning comeback
item.description: First-round vote raises prospect of dramatic victory for Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Will Germany come back to nuclear energy?
item.description: Germany shut down its last nuclear power plants in 2023 but as the pro-atom far-right Alternative for Germany gains broader support, the country might change course.

item.title: [Financial Times] Saudi Aramco chief warns world’s oil stockpiles are ‘scarily thin’
item.description: Amin Nasser says inventories depleted by Middle East conflict could take up to two years to rebuild

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia is losing its grip on Kaliningrad, despite using the exclave for anti-Nato scare stories
item.description: Nuclear sabre-rattling only underlines the fragility of Russia’s grip on its trophy territory.

item.title: [Financial Times] Flávio Bolsonaro takes commanding lead in Brazil election
item.description: Son of jailed former far-right president in pole position against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

item.title: [Financial Times] Euro slides to 17-month low against dollar
item.description: High energy prices and concerns over France’s public finances add to pressure on the single currency

item.title: [Politico Europe] Is Kemi Badenoch abandoning the Red Wall?
item.description: Is Andy Burnham an easier opponent for the Conservatives than Sir Keir Starmer? At the Tory conference in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch’s team sniff a chance to attack the prime minister – with a particular chance to seize on and attack his economic argument. Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy pore over Badenoch’s “The Right Way” pamphlet […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europe’s last socialist heavyweight Sánchez calls snap Spanish elections for Nov. 29
item.description: With housing topping voters’ concerns, the prime minister is hoping the affordability crisis can help him defy the polls and extend his time in power.

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: EU trade chief heads to China as Brussels unveils long-delayed pre-enlargement reforms
item.description: The European Commission is expected to present its long-delayed pre-enlargement policy reviews to prepare for the integration of Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine and Moldova.

item.title: [Politico Europe] The race for the EU’s plum diplomatic jobs begins
item.description: The race for some of the EU’s most coveted diplomatic jobs is under way. Zoya Sheftalovich and Nick Vinocur unpack why this year’s routine EEAS rotation is attracting unusually strong interest from senior Commission officials — and what it says about the mood in Brussels. Then, we head to France, where a wave of student […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Russia’s new drive to crush Ukraine
item.description: Moscow’s relentless offensive on cities and ports has halted the country’s grain exports, severing an economic lifeline

item.title: [Financial Times] Why a booming economy is not helping Trump
item.description: Anxiety about AI and affordability has turned his populist party into a popular target

item.title: [Financial Times] Estonia shifts troops closer to Russia in ‘active defence’ push
item.description: Baltic state prepares to carry out deep strikes inside its neighbour if it is attacked

item.title: [Politico Europe] Securing energy and trade flows in geo-economic conflicts
item.description: The Straight of Hormuz’s closure this year highlighted the fragility of trade routes and the Middle East’s importance for supplying the world. What can be done to be better in securing exports?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Push to ban EU left group over French riots
item.description: The European Left Alliance could face European Parliament vote this month after ECR starts gathering signatures.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Deutschland im Verteidigungsmodus
item.description: Friedrich Merz reist überraschend am Wochenende nach Kiew, ausgerechnet während massiver russischer Drohnenangriffe. Am heutigen Montag danach werden die Chefs der deutschen Nachrichtendienste wohl deutlich: Wie nah ist der hybride Schattenkrieg bereits in Deutschland angekommen? POLITICO-Reporter Hans von der Burchard ordnet ein, welche Botschaften der Kanzler aus der Ukraine mitbringt und was die öffentliche Anhörung […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Warum europäische KI allein keine Souveränität garantiert
item.description: POLITISCHE WERBUNG Weitere Informationen hier.

item.title: [DW] Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
item.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

item.title: [DW] EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
item.description: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

item.title: [EU Observer] G7 releases diesel stocks after Trump pressure, EU denies caving
item.description: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of emergency oil and fuel stocks after weeks in which Washington pressed European capitals to open their diesel reserves. Brussels said US threats played no part.

item.title: [EU Observer] The war changes yet again: Ukrainians use domestic missile for first time as Russians launch assault on bridges (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,681)
item.description: A defence analyst warned that Russia is mass-producing "thousands" of new drones “far more dangerous and faster" than jet-powered Shaheds which Ukraine cannot yet stop.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brunner takes victory lap on irregular arrivals as Syrian asylum claims collapse for reasons beyond EU policy
item.description: Syria's regime collapsed in December 2024, over 22 months ago. The country was the largest source of irregular arrivals in 2023. Today, the EU disingenuously attributes its migration policies for the drop of arrivals.

item.title: [EU Observer] French far-right leader Bardella denies writing antisemitic messages
item.description: Jordan Bardella, a leader of the French far-right National Rally, has denied writing antisemitic messages in 2013.

item.title: [EU Observer] Magyar waives his own immunity, as Hungary targets billions in alleged fraud and two former Orbán ministers in custody (Day 143 of the Tisza government)
item.description: PM Peter Magyar waives his own immunity as Hungary's "Operation Purgatory" saw authorities detain two former Orbán ministers over alleged multibillion-forint corruption. The new asset recovery office took over four major cases, including Orbán's brother's visa business, while Hungary may soon join the European Public Prosecutor's Office.
